correctness.rationale: The density-tail estimate has a controlled relative error \(m/(u-m)^2\), which tends to zero because the rare centering satisfies \((u-m)/\sqrt m\to\infty\). Independent Gamma maxima then have a common local exponential scale and an adjacent-shape tail ratio. The rate-function bound \(u/b^2\le2\log n+O(1)\) controls global Poisson-clock fluctuations for every divergent multiplicity sequence; last-completer ordering is preserved exactly. A standalone checker reproduced 454 finite assertions, which supplement but do not replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: A one-copy quota difference is the smallest natural heterogeneity in coupon collection. The theorem distinguishes a dominant high-quota class from a balanced last-completer competition at the critical ratio \(m/\log n\), with an explicit continuous transition. The universal completion-time Gumbel law holds without assuming the ratio converges; the joint competing-extremes profile determines which subsystem controls the final bottleneck.
